anuṭṭhāna:

jāli:
1jāli(n)

Vv 81:16 (mudūhi pāṇīhi ~ehi ca, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee jāla-; Vv-a 315,.30 foll. : jālavantehi abhilohitanakhehi, tena jālahatthataṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ tambanakhataṃ anuvyañjanaṃ ca dasseti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee jālihatthataṃ).

2jāli(n)
mfn. [from jāla2], possessing flames; S I 69,22* (pahūtabhakkhaṃ ~inaṃ pāvakaṃ kaṇhavattaniṃ daharo ti nāvajāneyya).
jātiya:
jātika

[BHS -jātika, -jātīya], ifc 1. of such a birth; of such a class; born from …; — see ahi-, eka-, kiṃ- (sv ka3), khattiya-, caṇḍāla-, jāti- (sv jāti1), taṇhā-, dīgha-, du-j-, nāmarūpa- (sv nāma2), nīca-, brāhmaṇa-, samāna- (sv samāna2), suci-, hīna- (sv jahati); — 2. of such a kind; of such a disposition, being by nature …; naturally disposed to; — see adhivāsaka-, apparajakkha-, alasa-, evaṃ-, kalyāṇa-, cintaka-, cokkha-, dabba- (sv dabba3), dubbaca- (sv vaca[s]), dhāraka-, nāgarika-, nirati-, nisāmaka-, maṇḍana-, mātugāma- (sv māta[r]1), māna- (sv māna1), huṃhuṅka-; — see also catujātiyagandha (sv catu[r]).

2jātiya
mfn. or m. [cf S. jātya?], being of such a kind, of such a class;? None;? A I 162,16* (evam eva manussesu yasmiṃ kasmiñci ~e khattiye brāhmaṇe vesse sudde caṇḍālapukkuse, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se jātiyaṃ; Mp II 258,.27 : yattha katthaci kule jāte) = III 214,6* (eds so).
nikkha:
1nikkha
n. [cf S. nikṣa, mfn.; or = nikkha2], a kiss;? Sadd 329,.26 (nikkha cumbane: nikkhati ~aṃ).

2nikkha

3nikkha
n. [from *ni2 + khaṇati? cf S. niṣkhanati], a water channel; Ja IV 358,29* (imāni tāni khettāni imaṃ ~aṃ sukuṇḍalaṃ; 359,8´ : imaṃ ~an ti imaṃ tādisam eva udakaniddhamanaṃ).
ogādha:
1ogādha
m. [cf S. gādha; BHS (SWTF) avagādha], firm footing in water, firm ground; ford; Ud-a 345,.21 (ogādhanti patiṭṭhahanti etena ettha vā ti ~o, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ogadhanti … ogadho); —      °-ppatta,   mfn., having gained a firm footing; A III 297,.15 (na imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ~ā paṭigādhappattā assāsappattā; cf Mp III 349,.26 : ~ā ti ogādhaṃ anupavesaṃ pattā); Spk I 295,.4 (~ā paṭigādhappattā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ogadhappattā); — see also ogadha1, ogādha2, ogādhati.

2ogādha

2okāra
m. [from *o2 + karoti? cf BHS avakāra, okāra], degradation, demeaning; Vin I 15,.37 (kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ ~aṃ saṅkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi) = D I 110,.3 (Sv 277,.28 : ~an ti avakāraṃ lāmaka-bhāvaṃ) = Ud 49,.7 (Ud-a 282,.28 : ~an ti lāmakasabhāvaṃ aseṭṭhehi sevitabbaṃ seṭṭhehi na sevitabbaṃ nihīna-sabhāvan ti attho); M I 115,.35 (addasaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ādīnavaṃ ~aṃ saṅkilesaṃ; Ps II 82,.18 : ~an ti lāmakabhāvaṃ, khandhesu vā ~aṃ, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be otāraṃ; cf vokāra); Nett 42,.1; — see also apakāra, avakāra1.

paḷāsa, palāsa

[cf BHS pradāsa], envious rivalry, emulation; asserting one’s equal merits; D II 342,.16 (makkhena pi naṃ harissāmi ~ena pi naṃ harissāmī ti); M I 15,.35 (makkho ca pāpako ~o ca pāpako; Ps I 106,.28 : yugaggāhalakkhaṇo ~o paraguṇehi attano guṇānaṃ samīkaraṇaraso paresaṃ guṇappamāṇena upaṭṭhānapaccupaṭṭhāno); A V 39,.33 (~o bhikkhave n’ eva kāyena pahātabbo no vācāya paññāya disvā disvā pahātabbo); Vv 15:5 (issā ca maccheram atho ~o; Vv-a 71,.13 : kulapadesādinā parehi yugaggāhalakkhaṇo ~o); Nidd I 13,.17; Vibh 357,.19 foll. (Be, Ce, Se so; Ee palāsākāro … yuddhaggāho …); Mil 289,.10; Vism 107,.1 (dosacaritassa kodho upanāho makkho ~o issā macchariyan ti); Mp II 162,.30 (yugaggāhalakkhaṇo ~o); —    apaḷāsa, apalāsa, m. and mfn., 1. (mfn.) without envious rivalry; A I 199,8* (~o asāhaso); — nippaḷāsa, mfn., without envious rivalry; Kv 606,.14 (nanu arahā nirāgo … nimmakkho nippaḷāso); — sapalāsa, mfn., full of envious rivalry; Kv 606,.10.
paribhāsana:

ind. [absol. of pacceti1 qv; BHS pratītya], 1. (+ acc.) relying on; dependent on; because of; produced from; (absolutely) in dependence; with a cause; Vin III 21,.17 (bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpessāmi dasa atthavase paṭicca; Sp 223,.29 : paṭicca āgamma ārabbha); IV 113,.10 (so anādariyaṃ paṭicca karoti yeva); D II 142,.24 (idaṃ kho Ānanda atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho); 302,.20 (bhikkhu cakkhuṃ ca pajānāti rūpe ca pajānāti yaṃ ca tadubhayaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṃyojanaṃ taṃ ca pajānāti); M I 85,.28 (yaṃ … ime pañca kāmaguṇe paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ); 295,.33 foll. (telappadīpassa jhāyato acciṃ paṭicca ābhā paññāyati ābhaṃ paṭicca acci paññāyati); 487,.20 (ayaṃ aggi tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca jalatī ti); S I 134,25* (hetuṃ paṭicca sambhūtaṃ hetubhaṅgā nirujjhati); II 86,.9 foll. (telaṃ ca paṭicca vaṭṭiṃ ca paṭicca telappadīpo jhāyeyya); IV 68,.7 (aniccaṃ … paccayaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ); V 64,.14 (ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati anāhāro no tiṭṭhati); A I 122,.5 (imaṃ kho bhikkhave puggalaṃ paṭicca dhammadesanā anuññātā); 209,.1 foll. dhammanisāmanā:
1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
